newsitem.title: PERU: Peru police unsure who exploded two bombs in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Peru police unsure who exploded two bombs in Lima.

text.p: Police had not determined early on Thursday who exploded package bombs outside two private homes in Lima, although the methods were the same as those used by Peru's leftist rebels.
"The methods used make one think that they could be terrorists," an anti-terrorist police officer told Reuters.

But the officer, who requested anonymity, said no fliers or graffitti were found at either site and there was not enough evidence to blame the bombings on Maoist Shining Path or pro-Cuban Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels.
He said bombs also are sometimes used by common criminals, including drug traffickers.

The package bombs went off almost simultaneously Wednesday night at homes in separate parts of Lima, blowing out windows, damaging doors and cars and injuring three people including a two-month-old girl, police and radio reports said.

The first bomb exploded at about 11:15 p.m. Wednesday (0415 GMT Thursday) in the poor San Martin de Porres district in front of the home of car salesmen Luis Ramos, badly damaging a house and injuring his daughter.
"They placed a bomb in front of my house," Ramos told Radioprogramas del Peru. "I don't know why. My 2-month-old baby girl was left unconcious."

The radio, quoting police at the scene, said the first bomb was made of 28 ounces (800 grams) of dynamite and fertiliser. The blast damaged buildings for several hundred feet around the site, also injuring two others.
The explosion occurred half a block from the home of pro- government Congressman Virgilio Gutierrez, who arrived home 30 minutes after the blast.
"I really don't think it could have been directed at me because I have never received any kind of threat," Gutierrez told Reuters.
"As a congressmen, I try to keep a low profile. I think it was just a coincidence..., although with these bombings you never know, right?," he added.
Minutes after the first explosion, a second package bomb exploded outside a house in the Peruvian capital, shattering windows.
Local radio said no one was injured by the second bomb, which was detected by the homeowner's dog.
"The dog was scratching at the door and we went to the door and found a white bag with the explosive," the owner's son, Jose Enrique Torres, told Radioprogramas del Peru.
"A child was watching and we pushed him out of the way so he wouldn't get hurt. We got back into the house and that's when it blew up."
The bombings came a day after suspected leftist rebels tossed a bag bomb at an electric company in northern Lima.
There were no injuries in Tuesday's bombing.
